summary: Kickoff for a 3-week pilot to validate Quantale Retail's checkout assistance model. Focused on quality evaluation (anchor prompts, regression set), hallucination and format checks, and end-to-end latency/cost benchmarks under production-like traffic. Agreement to run a controlled benchmark window mid-December and to reconvene on results + next steps for Dedicated capacity by 2028-01-05.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-02
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 1h12m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Quantale Head of Product), Samir (Quantale ML Platform), Olivia (Quantale Data Eng), Markus (Quantale Procurement)
Shared links: Pilot deck (drive.google.com/quantale-pilot-deck), Bench spreadsheet (sheets.google.com/quantale-bench), Security brief (redwood.com/security/brief)

---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro round, then we'll run through scope and success criteria for the pilot. Ethan and I will cover benchmarks and the eval plan.
[00:28] Lena (Quantale): Hi, thanks. Quick context: we want to roll out a checkout assistant to reduce support tickets and increase conversions. We're cautious about hallucinations and response formatting because downstream systems ingest structured answers.
[00:45] Samir (Quantale): Also latency under peak holiday load is non-negotiable, that's why we're exploring a POC that measures both quality and perf.
[01:05] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great, makes sense. We'll propose a three-week sprint: week one prep + anchor prompt set, week two bench runs, week three regression and gating. Open to adjusting timelines.
[01:30] Olivia (Quantale): Sounds tight but doable. We can ship a sample payload and a 7-day traffic slice. We'll need clear success metrics to sign off.
[01:50] Maya: Perfect. Let's start success criteria — what would make this pilot a go/no-go for you?
[02:05] Lena: For product, primary is accuracy on intention extraction and no critical hallucinations. If more than 3% of answers introduce fabricated product info that could drive an order, that's a fail. Also JSON output strictness — the format has to validate against our schema with < 1% structure errors.
[02:40] Samir: From infra side, P99 latency under 250ms for single-turn lookups at our normal batch size; during peak test window, P95 under 420ms. Cost is secondary for pilot but we want ballpark per-1M token projection.
[03:05] Markus: Legal/procurement need an audit log and an outline of data residency/KMS for the pilot. We won't sign PO until procurement sees security checklist.
[03:28] Maya: Okay noted. So success criteria summary: accuracy/hallucination thresholds, schema/format validation, latency SLOs, and security/KMS audit. We'll capture those in the pilot doc.

--- Topics: anchor prompts, regression suite, hallucination checks, scoring, benchmark windows, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated)

[04:00] Ethan: Diving into the quality eval plan. We suggest three tiers: anchor prompts (a small curated set — 120 examples representing prioritized flows), regression corpus (1,200+ cases including edge/failure modes), and randomized production slices for sampling. Anchor prompts are runtime seeds used for continuous smoke checks.
[04:35] Lena: Are anchor prompts the same as golden prompts? We call them anchor here.
[04:40] Ethan: Yeah similar idea; we prefer "anchor" for internal clarity. These will be manually labeled by your SMEs so scoring is deterministic.
[04:52] Olivia: For regression, we want synthetic fuzz cases — like partial SKUs, weird user punctuation, currency localizations — to see format robustness.
[05:10] Ethan: We'll also include negative tests that intentionally trigger hallucination e.g., SKU lookup for nonexistent SKUs, and expect a defined fallback response.
[05:25] Samir: How will scoring work? Do you do automated QA or manual labeling?
[05:30] Maya: Hybrid. Automated checks for schema/format (regex/jsonschema), automated heuristics for hallucination using knowledge-base matching, and manual review for subtle semantic errors. We'll provide an evaluation spreadsheet with columns for anchor expected output, auto-score, and manual notes.
[06:00] Lena: Can you quantify the auto-scoring thresholds?
[06:05] Ethan: For format: pass/fail JSON schema. For hallucination: token-level novelty score against your product KB; we flag anything with >15% novel factual tokens. For semantic intent accuracy: we'll use a weighted F1 against labeled anchors with a target of >= 0.87 for pilot success. Those thresholds are negotiable.
[06:45] Olivia: That 15% novelty metric — does it handle paraphrases?
[06:50] Ethan: Good question. Our KB matching uses fuzzy matching and entity reconciliation; paraphrases on intent won't trigger a hallucination flag unless they invent facts that don't map to KB entries. It's not perfect — that's where manual review comes in.

[07:20] Lena: What about regression cadence? After initial bench, we want daily smoke on anchors during the pilot and regression run nightly.
[07:30] Maya: Agreed. We'll set up a daily check that posts a short report to the Slack channel.

--- Benchmarks and workload sizing
[07:55] Ethan: For the perf bench, we propose two windows: baseline quiet period (50qps sustained) and a peak simulation (burst to 300qps for 10 minutes) to emulate Black Friday microbursts. We'll run both on the same model variants to compare hosted vs a quantized dedicated variant.
[08:25] Samir: How do you simulate our request shapes? We're multi-part payloads with metadata and KV cache keys.
[08:35] Ethan: We ask you to provide the sample payloads (anonymized) and a traffic distribution histogram; we'll replay at your VPC boundary. The bench script supports prefix caching toggles and continuous batching sim. Note: transcription might mis-say this as "cash" or "cache" sometimes.
[08:55] Olivia: We'll anonymize and drop PHI. Expect to see nested metadata fields.
[09:05] Ethan: Good. We'll map those to realistic token lengths and sequence lengths. For SLOs, we'll look at throughput per GPU and cost per 1k tokens at the observed batching footprint.
[09:30] Lena: Will you compare different quantization levels? We want to know quality vs. int8/int4 tradeoffs.
[09:38] Ethan: Yes. Part of the bench matrix: float16 baseline, int8 quantized, and an aggressive int4 where available. We'll run quality checks on the anchor prompts across each variant so you can see any regression in hallucination or format errors.

[10:00] Markus: Procurement question — if we decide dedicated, what is the minimum commitment and timeline?
[10:08] Maya: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-6 weeks after contract; for pilot we can run on hosted capacity. If Dedicated is chosen, we'll outline commit sizes in the proposal. We'll include cost estimates in the pricing sheet.

[10:35] Lena: Security: we need KMS in our cloud region, SOC 2 attestation and audit log retention for pilot. Do you offer a private control plane?
[10:46] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC peering, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and audit logs. For pilots we can enable per-request logging to your audit bucket with redaction. We'll attach a security brief.

[11:10] Ethan: Quick note on fallbacks: we'll configure graceful degradation rules — e.g., if model latency spikes beyond threshold, route to a cheaper model variant with a clear header in response so app can surface degraded mode to users.
[11:30] Samir: Good. We also want to measure token-level cost delta when using KV cache vs cold starts.
[11:38] Ethan: We'll include KV cache metrics and a run comparing cold/kvcached paths.

--- Sample scoring rubric (discussed)
[12:00] Ethan: Proposal for composite score: 60% semantic correctness (F1-like), 25% hallucination penalty, 15% format/schemas pass rate. We'll compute per-anchor and aggregate. Any anchor that falls below 0.6 composite triggers manual review and potential rollback.
[12:30] Lena: That composite seems reasonable; can we weight false positives more? We care about fabrication more than missing an optional field.
[12:40] Maya: Absolutely — we can change hallucination penalty weight if you prefer. We'll include a config file with weights you can tweak during pilot.

[13:00] Olivia: For manual labeling, who will do it? We'll repurpose part of our QA team. How long will labeling take?
[13:10] Ethan: For 120 anchors, manual labeling is around 6-8 hours for one SME. The 1,200 regression set will be sampled — automated filters will catch most. We'll share labeling templates.

[14:00] Lena: What about edge-case triggers and alerting thresholds — how will we surface regressions that only show up after a model swap?
[14:10] Ethan: We'll run nightly regression and send alerts if composite score drops by X% from the baseline. We'll also capture exemplar failures and paste into the shared sheet with context.

--- Timelines and milestones
[14:45] Maya: Proposed timeline:
- 2027-12-02: Kickoff (today)
- By 2027-12-07: Quantale provides sample payloads + list of high-risk flows
- 2027-12-09: Redwood delivers pilot plan, bench scripts, and initial anchor set
- Week of 2027-12-13: Bench window (baseline + peak)
- 2027-12-20: Regression run and preliminary results
- 2028-01-05: Decision checkpoint (go to dedicated / expand / cancel)

[15:35] Samir: That aligns with our holiday cadence; bench week before Christmas might be noisy but still workable.
[15:45] Markus: Procurement timeline — we can fast-track if we like the pilot. We'll start PO process after initial security docs.

--- Technical deep-dive snippets (SE-led)
[16:00] Ethan: On the bench harness: it's containerized, will run in your VPC via a transient runner. We support TLS mutual auth for replay, and store logs in S3 with lifecycle rules. Caching: prefix caching is enabled by default; we can toggle. Note: implementation doc is in the shared drive.
[16:35] Olivia: About payloads — some requests include customer embeddings and precomputed vectors, can your runtime accept pre-embedded vectors for reranking?
[16:45] Ethan: We currently accept embeddings for rerank workflows; we'll show end-to-end in the bench. If you plan to send precomputed vectors, include format spec in the sample.

[17:10] Lena: What if we see format regressions after a model update in production?
[17:15] Ethan: We'll set up a canary route for new model variants with a shadow traffic split. If format errors exceed thresholds, we automatically rollback.

[17:40] Maya: A few open Qs — can Redwood run QA on anonymized logs to identify hallucination hotspots?
[17:48] Ethan: Yes if you provide logs and consent. We'll run heuristics and tag potential hallucination clusters.

--- Natural transcription artifacts and small interruptions follow (a few overlapping voices, brief silence)

[18:10] Markus: Sorry, quick payments question — any PCI concerns?
[18:15] Maya: We don't store raw card data; we recommend tokenization at the app layer. We'll add that note to the security brief.

[18:45] Olivia: About scoring infra — do you provide the evaluation dashboard?
[18:50] Ethan: Yes. We'll provide a shared dashboard that shows composite scores by anchor, daily time series, and a drilldown to individual failures. We'll attach dashboards to the bench spreadsheet.

[19:20] Lena: On hallucination examples, can you surface the top 10 hallucination patterns?
[19:26] Ethan: We'll cluster and present top patterns with exemplar inputs and model outputs.

--- Closing recap
[20:00] Maya: To recap:
- Deliverables: pilot plan + bench scripts (Redwood), sample payloads + high-risk flows (Quantale).
- Bench windows: week of Dec 13 (baseline + peak).
- Quality eval: anchor set + regression set + nightly smoke; composite scoring (60/25/15) with adjustable weights.
- Security: provide KMS / audit doc; Redwood to attach security brief.
- Procurement: Markus to start checklist.

[20:40] Lena: Looks good. We'll try to get payloads to you by the 7th.
[20:45] Markus: I'll start procurement and share the PO template.
[20:48] Maya: Great, we'll share the pilot proposal and pricing by Monday 2027-12-06. Ethan will send the bench harness and labeling templates by Thursday 2027-12-09.

[21:05] Ethan: One last note on hallucination scoring — we'll include a human-review override so if automated heuristics flag false positives, you can correct labels and retrain the metric.

[21:25] Olivia: That helps. Also please include an example of an expected fallback response for missing SKUs.

[21:40] Maya: Noted. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the shared thread.

[21:55] Meeting end.
